title: Conformalized time-series foundation models for commodity prices: replication material

creators.name: Ahn, Suho
creators.affiliation: Department of Business and Technology Management, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea

description:
Replication material for the paper "Conformalized time-series foundation models for commodity prices: an econometric audit across crisis regimes".

Five time-series foundation models (Chronos-Bolt small and base, Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Moirai-2) are audited on ten daily commodity futures over 2015–2026 against a classical econometric panel, under a Model Confidence Set, with predictive-interval coverage evaluated inside named crisis regimes and backtested as value-at-risk, and validated on a holdout window covering the 2026 Iran–Hormuz shock that was sealed before any model was run and evaluated exactly once.

This archive contains: cached forecasts for all 361 model–series–horizon combinations (no GPU required to check the paper's numbers); the evaluation code, statistical tests and conformal prediction constructions; information-set leakage tests that verify no future information enters an interval; the frozen pre-registration with its complete deviation log; the pre-committed interpretation of every possible holdout outcome, written before unsealing; and the audit trail of the single-use holdout evaluation.

Licensing is mixed: code is released under the MIT License; result files, tables and figures under CC BY 4.0; raw price data under the terms of its original public sources, documented per series in data/DATA_SOURCES.md. Third-party model weights are not redistributed — the Hugging Face checkpoint identifiers are recorded in the README.

Version 1.1.1. Adds the robustness analyses prompted by a pre-submission review: a sweep of trailing conformal window lengths {50, 100, 250, 500} and adaptive step sizes {0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05}, and value-at-risk backtests repeated on non-overlapping forecast origins. The interpretation of every possible sweep outcome was recorded before any output existed.

These analyses did not confirm the earlier framing. Two claims were withdrawn and three narrowed, and the deviation log records this with the date. Withdrawn: that adaptive conformal inference is the best construction at every horizon and regime (a 50-observation trailing window attains 0.800 against a nominal 0.80 at h = 1 in the COVID window, where the adaptive layer reaches 0.770); and that the panel fails the value-at-risk backtest at the monthly horizon (an artefact of overlapping forecasts — on non-overlapping origins only full fine-tuning fails). Narrowed: the crisis failure of the trailing-window baseline is substantially a property of the 250-observation window length rather than of non-adaptive calibration in general, and the width premium of the adaptive layer is 44% at the monthly horizon rather than the 25% previously quoted from the weekly horizon. Also reported: the pre-registered step size was not the best available value, and is nonetheless retained as the headline configuration.

What survives is a claim about stability rather than dominance: no fixed calibration window is adequate across horizons and regimes, while a single adaptive step size holds coverage within 0.044 of nominal in all nine horizon-by-regime cells, against 0.121 for the best fixed window. No forecast, result file, evaluation script or number from v1.0.0 was altered.

v1.1.1 corrects the README, which in v1.1.0 still described claims that the sensitivity analyses in that same release had withdrawn. No data, code or result file changed between the two.
